<a id="set-curtain-wall-embed"></a>

### Set curtain wall embed

**DRAFT - not yet usable in a chat - refused until proved (D-117).**

**What it does:** make this curtain wall cut the wall it is drawn in - tick or untick Automatically Embed on its type, and read back which walls it cuts.

TICKS OR UNTICKS AUTOMATICALLY EMBED (Type Properties > Construction) on the type of each curtain wall picked, so that it cuts an opening in the wall it is drawn in, or stops. **THE BOX BELONGS TO THE TYPE, SO EVERYTHING SHARING IT CHANGES.** Each one picked is followed to its type, each type is written once, and the answer counts how many share it. One already set as asked is named in `alreadyThat` and not written. Anything picked that is not a curtain wall - the brick wall itself, say - is named in `notCurtain` and left alone. **WHAT IT CUTS IS READ OFF THE MODEL.** Every wall whose box meets each one picked is asked what it holds inside it, before and after, so the answer lists what it cut before and what it cuts now. ASSUMPTION for the proof: whether ticking the box affects one already drawn, or only those drawn after, has not been measured - the before-and-after says which, and nothing is claimed beyond it. `embed` is yes or no. The box is found by Revit's own built-in id, never by its name. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16). Every refusal is made before the first write; a type that refuses it, or reads back otherwise after one regeneration, stops the call and nothing it did is kept. In a shared model a type another user holds is refused naming them.

<a id="set-curtain-wall-grid"></a>

### Set curtain wall grid

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-02 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** set how a curtain wall type's grid lines are laid out and spaced, each way.

Sets a curtain wall TYPE's grid - the Layout and the Spacing of its Vertical Grid, its Horizontal Grid, or both, which is what Type Properties shows under those two headings. Only what the modeller names changes: a direction, or a setting, left out of the request is left exactly as it is. **IT CHANGES THE TYPE, SO EACH WALL BUILT FROM IT CHANGES TOO.** The walls using it are counted before anything is written, and the count is the first line of the answer - "used by 12 walls - every one of them changed with the type". To change one wall alone, DUPLICATE_TYPE first, put that wall on the copy with CHANGE_ELEMENT_TYPE, and set the copy. **THE TYPE IS NAMED IN THE REQUEST** - "Curtain Wall: Storefront", or the bare type name when no other wall type shares it (D-54). The change is a type change, and naming the type keeps that in the request itself; one wall clicked on screen would read as "this wall" and change a hundred. REPORT_CURTAIN_ELEMENTS on one curtain wall prints its name, which for a wall is its type's. A wall type that is not a curtain wall - a basic or a stacked one - is refused by name and nothing is changed. **WHY NOT WRITE_ELEMENT_PARAMETERS.** "Layout" and "Spacing" each appear twice on a curtain wall type, once per direction, and a lookup by name picks one of the two with no rule for which - so that fragment refuses the name (D-54 s3, FRAGMENT-ISSUES 5b-203). This reaches each setting by Revit's own parameter id, SPACING_LAYOUT_VERT and _HORIZ and SPACING_LENGTH_VERT and _HORIZ, so there is no name to confuse. **THE REQUEST IS A SHORT TABLE** - "vertical layout=fixed distance; vertical spacing=1500". Four settings can be named: vertical layout, vertical spacing, horizontal layout, horizontal spacing. A layout is none, fixed distance, maximum spacing or minimum spacing. A spacing is MILLIMETRES (D-71), digits only, converted to Revit's feet once, here; at least 100 and at most 100,000, because below that a number typed in metres - 1.5 for 1500 - would put a line every 1.5 mm on each wall built from the type. A spacing is taken only with a layout that uses one: under None there are no lines to space, and a spacing that would change nothing is refused rather than written and reported as done. A direction's layout is written before its spacing, so a layout and a spacing asked together work on a type whose layout was None. **FIXED NUMBER IS REFUSED, AND THAT IS THE BOUNDARY.** Under Fixed Number the COUNT is not on the type: Revit shows it as "Number" in each placed WALL's own Properties, so a type change cannot say how many, and each wall built from the type would switch to a count nobody chose. Asking for it refuses the whole request and changes nothing. Where Revit keeps that count - and each wall's Justification, Angle and Offset - is MEASURED on every run and printed in `readBack`, so the first proof records it rather than this card asserting it. **IT REPORTS WHAT REVIT HOLDS, NOT WHAT WAS ASKED.** After the write the walls are rebuilt and every grid setting of the type is read back, both directions, beside what it was before. A layout is stored as a whole number, and the number written is Revit's SpacingRuleLayout value - None 0, Fixed Distance 1, Fixed Number 2, Maximum Spacing 3, Minimum Spacing 5, read off all eight releases' assemblies; there is no 4. That this parameter uses those numbers is an ASSUMPTION until a proof reads it back, so each layout is also read as Revit displays it: one displayed as a different layout from the one written stops the call and nothing is kept, and one displayed in words this does not recognise - a Revit in another language - is named in `differs` and not counted. Where a wall of the type is placed, one wall is measured before and after: its grid lines counted by the way each one actually runs - never by Revit's U and V names, which its reference does not tie to vertical or horizontal on a wall - and its mullions counted by type. **A CURTAIN SYSTEM'S TOO (version 3)** - its Grid 1 and Grid 2: grid 1 layout, grid 1 spacing, grid 2 layout, grid 2 spacing. The comments above `version` say how they are reached and what is assumed. **AND THE TYPE'S MULLIONS (version 4)** - Interior, Border 1 and Border 2 for the Vertical and Horizontal Mullions, in a second short table: "vertical interior=Rectangular Mullion: 50 x 150mm; horizontal border 2=none". A mullion type is named, and the name has to mean exactly one in the model - a name that matches none is refused with the mullion types the model has, two refused naming both. "none" takes the mullions off a position and is the only word that does; a blank is refused. NOTHING IS LOADED: a mullion family not in the model is refused, because loading one brings its own materials. Either table may be left out, not both. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16). Every refusal is made before the first write. If Revit refuses a write, or cannot rebuild the walls with it, the call stops and nothing it did is kept - a type half-changed across the walls that use it is worse than one left alone.

|---|---|
| **Kind** | Changes the model (`MODIFY`) |
| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **You say** | **curtain wall type** - text<br>**grid** - name=value, SEMICOLONS between - "view=*-Mech*; sheet=A-*"; a value holding a ";" goes in double quotes - Note="a; b"; optional, left out means *;*<br>**mullions** - name=value, SEMICOLONS between - "view=*-Mech*; sheet=A-*"; a value holding a ";" goes in double quotes - Note="a; b"; optional, left out means *;* |
| **You get** | applied, differs, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2024 |
| **Capability** | `SET_CURTAIN_WALL_GRID` |

<a id="set-element-level"></a>

### Set element level

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-24 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** reassign these to a different level without moving them.

Moves elements onto a different level **while keeping them physically where they are** — the coordination fix for services modelled against the wrong level, which is common and invisible until somebody schedules by level. **This is the fragment with the trap in it, and the trap is the whole point.** An element's height is stored as an OFFSET from its level. Change the level and leave the offset, and the element JUMPS by the difference between the two levels — a duct at 2800 above Level 1 becomes a duct 2800 above Level 2, three metres higher, silently. So the offset is recomputed so the absolute height is unchanged. **The absolute height is read before and verified after**, because a recomputation that is merely written is not one that took. **WALLS TOO, BOTH ENDS** (version 2, when SET_WALL_CONSTRAINTS was merged in). A wall's base goes to the level given, its base offset re-solved so the wall does not move; its top goes to `topLevelId` when one is named, its top offset re-solved the same way. `keepWallBase` leaves every wall's base alone, so the tops can be tied on their own. A wall whose top is UNCONNECTED has no top level - giving it one is a design change, so it is named in `unconnectedTop` and skipped unless `allowUnconnectedToBecomeBound` says so. A top level id that is not a level refuses the whole call, and what is not a wall is named in `notAWall`. A write that fails part-way is put back, never left half-set. **COLUMNS TOO, BOTH ENDS** (version 3). An architectural or structural column takes the wall's rule: its base to the level given unless `keepWallBase`, its top to `topLevelId`, each offset re-solved so the column stays where it is. An end attached to a roof, floor or beam is set by what it is attached to, so that column is refused with the reason; one with no top level has its top named in `unconnectedTop`. `columnReport` says what each column's two ends were and are now. **Reassigning and moving are opposite intentions said the same way.** *"Put these on Level 2"* can mean re-label them or physically raise them. `MOVE_ELEMENTS` and `ALIGN_ELEMENTS` are the ones that move; this one deliberately does not. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

The field's own name says which kind; optional, left out means *none*<br>**keep wall base** - yes or no - true or false; optional<br>**allow unconnected to become bound** - yes or no - true or false; optional |
| **You get** | moved, height changed |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2024 |
| **Capability** | `SET_ELEMENT_LEVEL` |

<a id="set-element-workset"></a>

### Set element workset

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-14 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** move these elements onto a different workset.

Puts elements on a named workset. On a shared job that is how services get handed between disciplines and how a model stays openable — and elements modelled on the wrong workset is one of the commonest things found at a coordination review. **It reports what CHANGED, and an element already on that workset is counted separately.** "Moved 200" when 190 were already there is the failure this project keeps meeting. **An element owned by another user cannot be moved and it fails at the write.** `REPORT_ELEMENT_OWNERSHIP` is the fragment that turns that into a sentence beforehand rather than a batch that stops at the eleventh — this one reports the refusal it hits. **A workset is not a phase, a design option or a filter**, and all four get described as "which one it belongs to". Only this one decides who can edit it and whether it loads when the model opens. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="set-mullion-join"></a>

### Set mullion join

**DRAFT - not yet usable in a chat - refused until proved (D-117).**

**What it does:** make these mullions continuous through the crossing, or break them at the join - Revit's Make Continuous and Break at Join.

SETS HOW MULLIONS MEET WHERE THEY CROSS - Revit's Make Continuous, the mullion running through the crossing, and Break at Join, the mullion stopping at the one it meets. "Make this mullion continuous", "break this mullion at the join", "make the vertical mullions run through the transoms". **THE MULLIONS HANDED IN, AND ONLY THOSE.** Any number, on any curtain walls; anything that is not a mullion is named in `notMullion` and left alone. `join` is continuous or break. Nothing on a type is written. **REVIT SAYS NOTHING BACK, SO EACH MULLION IS MEASURED.** Neither of Revit's calls returns anything, and a mullion has no setting to read back. So each one's length along its own run is measured off its solid before and after: made continuous it grows by the width of what it crosses, broken it shrinks. One that did not change the way asked is in `unchanged` with both lengths and never counted - it may already have been that way, may cross nothing, or the wall type's Join Condition may decide it. ASSUMPTION for the proof: that this length tells continuous from broken. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16). Every refusal is made before the first write; a mullion Revit will not take stops the call and nothing it did is kept. In a shared model a mullion another user holds is refused naming them.

| **You get** | changed, findings |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | none |
| **Capability** | `SET_MULLION_JOIN` |

<a id="set-pin-state"></a>

### Set pin state

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-09 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** pin these elements so they cannot be moved, or unpin them.

Pins or unpins elements. Pinning is how a modeller says "this is coordinated, leave it alone" - grids, levels, linked models and anything set out against another trade. **This fragment is the other half of a defect this repository already found.** Revit's move call returns normally and moves NOTHING for a pinned element, so MOVE_ELEMENTS has to probe positions before and after to tell moved from blocked. Pinning is the state that causes it, which makes reading and setting it the natural companion: "it did not move" and "it is pinned" are the same sentence from two ends. **It reports what CHANGED, never what was asked for.** An element already in the requested state is counted separately rather than added to the total, because "pinned 40" when 38 were already pinned is the exact failure shape this project keeps meeting. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

<a id="shape-wall-tops-to-roof"></a>

### Shape wall tops to roof

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-16 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** edit the profile of these walls so their tops follow the underside of the roof above, closing the gable.

Edits the profile of the walls selected so each wall's top follows the underside of the roof above it - Edit Profile, done for the modeller - and closes the open triangle under a gable. The roof's underside is measured every 50 mm along the wall on both its faces, and the lower kept, so the top never pokes through the roof; a ridge between two measurements is put where the slopes meet. The wall's bottom and ends stay as they were. **THE TOP IS A SKETCH AND DOES NOT FOLLOW THE ROOF.** If the roof moves or is rebuilt, the wall keeps the old outline - unlike Attach Top/Base. Every answer says so. From Revit 2025, ATTACH_WALLS attaches the wall instead. **REFUSED WITH THE REASON, and nothing on that wall changed:** a wall Revit says cannot have a profile sketch - in Revit's own words; a wall that already has an edited profile; a wall in a group; a wall the roof does not cover along its whole length. A roof in the selection is the one followed; with none, each wall finds the roof above it. **READ BACK.** The profile Revit holds after its edit mode closes must have a corner at every point of the roof's underside, to 1 mm; if not, the profile is removed again and the wall is as it was. **WHEN A ROOF WILL NOT JOIN.** Revit's API has no Join/Unjoin Roof on any release, so no tool makes that join (the `join-roofs` method). Where the walls under the roof are what has to meet it, this is the other way - offered, and run only on a yes. A roof by extrusion - or, from Revit 2022, a roof by footprint's gable end - is brought to another roof by EXTEND_ROOF_TO_ROOF; otherwise the join is done by hand: Modify > Join/Unjoin Roof.

<a id="slope-roof-edges"></a>

### Slope roof edges

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-11-16 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** slope the edges of this roof to make it a gable, a hip, or slope only the edges chosen.

Slopes the edges of a footprint roof that is already in the model, so a flat roof becomes a GABLE or a HIP at the pitch the modeller gives - or, since version 2, slopes only the EDGES the modeller names. It acts on the roof SELECTED in Revit - one CREATE_FLOOR made with a roof type, or one drawn by hand through Architecture > Roof by Footprint, which is the same kind of element. Several roofs may be selected; each is judged, sloped and read back on its own. **REVIT'S "SlopeAngle" IS NOT AN ANGLE.** The per-edge property holds a rise over a run - 0.5 is one unit up for every two across, 26.57 degrees. The pitch arrives in degrees and is turned into that ratio by its tangent before it is written: 30 degrees becomes 0.5774. Handed 30 straight through, Revit would build a roof 88 degrees steep and say nothing. So every edge is read back and turned back into degrees with the raw ratio printed beside it, and the roof's height is measured - the mistake would show twice over if it ever came back. **THE PITCH IS ALWAYS ASKED FOR AND NEVER ASSUMED (D-33).** CREATE_FLOOR refuses to invent one on a roof for the same reason: a default pitch becomes a pitch quietly relied on. It is in DEGREES, the usual way to state a pitch on a metric drawing. A ratio - "1 in 2" - is the other common way and is NOT read here, so that one number can never mean two things: convert it first (1 in 2 is 26.57 degrees). More than 0 and at most 80 degrees: 0 is the flat roof it already is, and 80 is a rise of 5.7 times the run, past any ordinary roof. A bigger number is refused rather than built, because a percentage or a height typed where degrees were asked is no pitch at all. **GABLE: THE TWO LONG SIDES SLOPE AND THE TWO ENDS STAY UPRIGHT.** Only on an outline of four straight sides in two parallel pairs, one pair longer than the other; a side drawn in collinear pieces still counts as one side. Anything else is REFUSED with the reason and that roof is not touched - an L-shaped outline has six sides and no single pair of eaves, a square has no LONG pair, and a curved edge is no eave. Heron does not choose two edges for the modeller. **HIP: EVERY EDGE SLOPES**, straight or curved, whatever the outline. **EDGES: ONLY THE EDGES NAMED SLOPE** (version 2), on any outline - a roof clipped to a valley, a lean-to with one sloping edge. Each edge is named by its number as readBack lists it; every edge not named stands upright. Asked with no numbers, or a number the roof has not got, nothing is changed and every edge is listed with its number, its length and its two ends, so the next ask can name them. One roof at a time: an edge number belongs to one roof. Numbers given with gable or hip are refused, never ignored. **ONE OUTLINE PER ROOF.** A footprint with a second loop - an opening, or a second roof area drawn in the same sketch - is refused for both shapes, since which loop is the eaves is not a thing to guess. **WHAT IS NOT A FOOTPRINT ROOF IS NAMED AND LEFT ALONE.** An extrusion roof takes its slope from the profile it was drawn with and has no footprint edges; a wall or a floor in the same selection is not a roof. A roof inside a group is refused before anything is attempted. **IT REPORTS WHAT REVIT HOLDS, NOT WHAT WAS ASKED.** After the write the roof is rebuilt and every edge is read back: whether it defines slope, and the slope in degrees. An edge holding anything else is named in `differs`, the way WRITE_ELEMENT_PARAMETERS names `snapped`. The roof is measured too - how far its highest point sits above its lowest, now and before - because an edge count cannot tell a 30 degree roof from an 88 degree one, and a height can. **IT DOES NOT TOUCH THE OVERHANG, THE OFFSET OR THE ROOF TYPE.** ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16). When Revit will not take a slope, or cannot rebuild the roof with it, the call stops and nothing it did is kept - a half-sloped roof is worse than none.

<a id="transfer-line-styles-between-documents"></a>

### Transfer line styles between documents

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-08 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** bring the line styles over from the other project.

Copies line styles from another OPEN project into this one - *"bring the line styles over from the template"*, *"get the line styles from last job"*. **A LINE STYLE IS A SUBCATEGORY, NOT AN ELEMENT, SO IT IS BUILT RATHER THAN COPIED.** Each one is a subcategory of the Lines category, and it is made here with `NewSubcategory` and then given the source's line weight, colour and pattern. That is why this fragment cannot lean on the document-to-document copy that `TRANSFER_VIEW_FILTERS_BETWEEN_DOCUMENTS` and `TRANSFER_VIEWS_BETWEEN_DOCUMENTS` use - there is no element to copy. **THE LINE PATTERN IS A SEPARATE ELEMENT, AND THAT IS WHERE THIS GOES WRONG QUIETLY.** A style whose pattern does not exist here lands **solid** - present, correctly named, right colour, right weight, and drawing the wrong thing. Nobody notices until a drawing is issued. So the pattern is matched by **name** in this project, and where it is missing the pattern element itself is brought over first. If even that fails the style is still created, left solid, and named in `weakened` rather than reported as created. **A style that arrived looking right and draws solid is the failure being guarded against.** **A NAME THAT ALREADY EXISTS HERE IS SKIPPED, NEVER OVERWRITTEN.** Two projects can hold a style with one name and different weights, and silently replacing this project's standards with another project's is worse than doing nothing. The name goes in `clashed` and the existing style is left exactly as it was. **BOTH PROJECTS MUST BE OPEN IN THE SAME REVIT.** The source is found by its title among the open documents; if it is not open, the open ones are listed and nothing is attempted. Linked documents are not offered - a link is reached through its `RevitLinkInstance`, and two links can share a title. **ONLY THE PROJECTION WEIGHT IS CARRIED.** A line style has no cut weight to copy; asking for one returns nothing useful on any release. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16). **The undo belongs to THIS document** - Rule 16 is per document, and the source project is only read.

|---|---|

| **Reached by** | asking in a Claude chat |
| **You say** | **source document title** - text<br>**name contains** - text |
| **You get** | created, weakened |
| **Built for Revit** | 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2027 |
| **Proved on Revit** | 2024 |
| **Capability** | `TRANSFER_LINE_STYLES_BETWEEN_DOCUMENTS` |

**How to use it**

1. Open the model in Revit and connect Heron: press **Heron** on the Heron tab, so its heron turns orange.
2. Turn **Changes** on in Heron's **Settings** (Heron tab).
3. In a Claude chat, ask in your own words, for example *"bring the line styles over from the template"*. Say the values under **You say** in the same sentence.
4. Heron makes the change as **one entry in Revit's Undo list**. With **Ask to Keep** on, Revit asks **Keep or Discard** first; Ctrl+Z takes it back.

<a id="transfer-materials-between-documents"></a>

### Transfer materials between documents

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-14 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** bring the materials over from the other project.

Copies materials from another OPEN project into this one - *"bring the materials over from the template"*, *"get the materials from last job"*. **A MATERIAL IS AN ELEMENT, so this is a document-to-document copy** - the same shape as `TRANSFER_VIEW_FILTERS_BETWEEN_DOCUMENTS`, and unlike `TRANSFER_LINE_STYLES_BETWEEN_DOCUMENTS`, where a style is a subcategory and has to be built. **WHAT A MATERIAL DRAGS BEHIND IT IS THE WHOLE PROBLEM.** A material is a thin thing pointing at several fat ones: an **appearance asset** (what it looks like rendered), a **thermal** and a **structural** asset, and up to four **fill patterns** for its surface and cut. Every one of those is a separate element. Revit usually brings them along; usually is not a word this library accepts, so each landed material is read back and compared against the source **property by property**, and anything that did not arrive is named in `weakened` rather than reported as copied. **THE APPEARANCE ASSET IS THE ONE THAT FOOLS PEOPLE.** A material that arrives without it keeps its shading colour, so it looks entirely correct in a shaded view, in every list, and in the material browser. It is wrong only in a **rendered or realistic** view - which is usually opened last, often by somebody else, and sometimes not before the images go out. **A NAME THAT ALREADY EXISTS HERE IS SKIPPED, NEVER OVERWRITTEN.** Two projects can hold "Concrete - Cast In Situ" with different patterns and different appearance assets, and quietly replacing this project's version changes how everything already using it draws and renders. The name goes in `clashed` and this project is left alone. **BOTH PROJECTS MUST BE OPEN IN THE SAME REVIT.** The source is found by its title among the open documents; if it is not open, the open ones are listed and nothing is attempted. Linked documents are not offered - a link is reached through its `RevitLinkInstance`, and two links can share a title. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16). **The undo belongs to THIS document** - the source project is only read.

<a id="transfer-object-styles-between-documents"></a>

### Transfer object styles between documents

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-10-28 (Revit 2020).

**What it does:** bring the object styles over from the other project.

Makes this project's Object Styles match another OPEN project's - *"bring the object styles over from the template"*, *"set the line weights up like the other job"*. Line weights, line colour, line pattern and material, for categories and their subcategories. **THIS ONE OVERWRITES, AND THAT IS THE DIFFERENCE FROM EVERY OTHER TRANSFER IN THIS LIBRARY.** Filters, line styles, parameters and materials all SKIP a name that is already here, because arriving twice is a mistake. Object styles are not like that: Walls exists in both projects, always, and the entire job is to change what Walls looks like here. So an existing category **is changed**, and every category actually changed is named in `changed` with what moved - because a transfer that silently restyles two hundred categories and reports a number is not something anybody can check. **NOTHING IS TOUCHED UNLESS IT DIFFERS.** A category whose settings already match the source is left alone and does not appear in `changed`, so the report is the diff rather than the inventory. **A MISSING SUBCATEGORY IS CREATED; A MISSING CATEGORY IS NOT.** A custom subcategory - a firm's own sub-style under Walls - is made here with `NewSubcategory` and then styled. A top-level category cannot be created at all: the set is Revit's, so one that is absent here is named in `skipped` rather than attempted. **THE MATERIAL AND THE LINE PATTERN ARE THE TWO THAT GO QUIET.** Both are separate elements, matched **by name** in this project - the same thing in two projects has two different ids, and an id carried across means nothing here. A line pattern that is missing is brought over as an element. A **material** is not: bringing a material over drags its appearance asset and its own patterns behind it, which is `TRANSFER_MATERIALS_BETWEEN_DOCUMENTS`'s whole job and not something to do as a side effect of styling a category. So a category whose material is not here keeps the material it had, and is named in `weakened` saying which material is missing and to run the materials transfer first. **BOTH PROJECTS MUST BE OPEN IN THE SAME REVIT**, and categories are matched by NAME - both documents are in the same Revit and therefore the same language, which is what makes that safe. If the source is not open, the open ones are listed and nothing is attempted. Linked documents are not offered. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16). **The undo belongs to THIS document** - the source project is only read. That matters more here than in the other transfers: this is the one that changes how the whole model draws, and one Ctrl+Z has to put all of it back.

<a id="ungroup-elements"></a>

### Ungroup elements

**Usable in a chat.** Proved on a real model on 2026-09-13 (Revit 2024).

**What it does:** break these groups apart into their members.

Breaks groups apart and hands back the elements that were inside them. **The commonest reason to reach for this is that something will not move.** A group member silently refuses to move — Revit's move returns normally and moves nothing — and ungrouping is one of the three fixes for "it will not move", the other two being unpinning and getting ownership. They look identical to the user and are not interchangeable. **Ungrouping one instance changes only that instance.** The group TYPE stays in the project and every other placed instance is untouched, which is what somebody expects and is worth stating because deleting the type is a different, much larger action. **The members come back, which is what makes this composable.** Ungroup and then move is a real two-step job, and the second step needs the elements the first one released. ASSUMES AN OPEN TRANSACTION and does not open one (Golden Rule 16).

**How to use it**

2. Select what it works on in Revit (elements) - or name it in the same request, and Heron finds it first.
